name: Amlodipine
sections: 408.88 g/mol (base); 567.05 g/mol (besylate; 6.94 mg besylate ≈ 5 mg base)
White crystalline powder (besylate), slightly soluble in water.

On the WHO List of Essential Medicines and one of the most prescribed drugs worldwide; ALLHAT and ASCOT-BPLA established its outcome benefits. First approval/introduction: Patented 1982; approved 1990 (Pfizer).

Inhibits transmembrane influx of calcium through L-type channels in vascular smooth muscle and myocardium, causing peripheral arterial vasodilation and reduced blood pressure; dilates coronary arteries and reduces myocardial oxygen demand in angina. Receptor / target profile: Long-acting dihydropyridine L-type calcium channel blocker selective for vascular smooth muscle.
Extensive hepatic (CYP3A4) to inactive pyridine metabolites
Summary: Bioavailability 64–90%; Tmax 6–12 h. ~97.5% protein bound. Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4). Half-life 30–50 h (once-daily).
Coronary artery disease (to reduce angina hospitalisation)
Hypertension / angina: 5 mg once daily; may increase to 10 mg once daily
Elderly, small or frail patients, hepatic impairment: 2.5 mg once daily
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use only if no safer alternative.
Obstruction of left ventricular outflow (e.g. severe aortic stenosis)
Haemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI
CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, ketoconazole, diltiazem) raise levels
With or without food; grapefruit may increase levels.
Marked peripheral vasodilation, hypotension, reflex tachycardia, shock. Supportive care; IV calcium gluconate; vasopressors.
ALLHAT (JAMA 2002) – amlodipine as effective as chlorthalidone for coronary outcomes.
ASCOT-BPLA (Lancet 2005) – amlodipine-based regimen reduced CV events and mortality versus atenolol-based.
Ankle swelling is common – report if severe
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
